# The result of the constructor of a BallVector: the radius given, or NaN

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `bv_make_finish` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The result of the constructor of a BallVector from its radius $r_z$ and the mask $\mathit{ok}$ that no center was a NaN: $r_z$ when $\mathit{ok}$ is true and $r_z$ is finite and not negative, with the flag $\mathit{flag}$ true; otherwise a NaN and the flag false, and the constructor returns the whole space:

$$r = r_z \ \text{when } \mathit{ok} \text{ is true and } r_z \text{ is finite} \text{ and } r_z \ge 0, \qquad r = \mathrm{NaN} \text{ otherwise}.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_make_1`, called by the constructors of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_make_2_entry`, called by the constructors of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- $r_z$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $\mathit{ok}$ is a mask, true or false.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{flag}$ is true exactly when $\mathit{ok}$ is true and $r_z$ is finite and not negative (a zero of either sign is not).
- When it is, $r = r_z$.
- Otherwise $r$ is a NaN.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `bv_make_finish_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBvNegMake.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBvNegMake.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions bv_make_finish_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `bv_make_finish_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the finish of a constructor: the radius given, or the canonical NaN (milestone2.md, BallVector, Values). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/bv_make_finish.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/bv_make_finish.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`norm_finish_1`](norm_finish_1.md).

```
# The finish of bv_make_k, the constructors of a BallVector (milestone2.md, "BallVector", "Values":
# "a constructor given a radius that is negative or a NaN, or a center that is not finite, returns the
# whole space"): norm_finish_1 under the state's mask and the test that the radius is not negative
# (le(0, rz), false for a NaN and for a negative number, true for either zero). The other ball vectors
# have norm_finish_1, which does not test the sign: their radii are nonnegative by construction. The
# claim says the test: finite_or_nan with nonneg.

p         = le(0, rz)
q         = and(ok, p)
(r, flag) = norm_finish_1(rz, q)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#bv_make_finish)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 1 991 824 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
